items.text: The post is Lamplighter orange, the kilometre stencilled twice. No plate. The lamp is lit on Ivy's schedule.
A brass plate sits over the second stencil, four screws, one steel. The lamp is still Ivy's.
CUT-19 reads in brass. The stencil underneath is colder. The lamp is still Ivy's.
The plate is gone. The stencil read again in a day. Overlay is short one post.
Brass over stencil, both visible. The post means two things, which is already its job.
The lobby timetable is pre-Exchange and wrong. The grease pencil is the document.
Overlay print over glass. The hand is paler underneath. HELD is not in the font.
Rolling stacks, most off their rails. The Garrison looked twice.
A hole in the grey brick. If an index came out, it is on a desk somewhere.
The half-sunk plate still shows REC-. The index stays in the geology.
The corridors still believe in authenticators.
The book is out, or copy, or refused. The visited column is honest.
The needle has hairline cracks and a stop painted by someone tired of replacing it.
Overlay lots on the beam. District 8 can pathfind by number. The needle has no opinion.
Mass only. Osric still writes kilograms.
A long table, scarred, benches both sides. Oil lamps with glass intact.
The ledger names people. The cross is still in it. The notice is face-down.
Four lanes narrowing to a booth that is not always staffed.
A clipboard calls it a friendly obstacle. D/9 marked the rail.
The housing was checked. The Tollman does not need to be present for the authority to work.
A gate frozen mid-cycle. Water-heights, dates.
COMPLETE brass on the leaf. The leaf is still where it stopped.
The gauges are filed. They believe the failure.
The plate is down. Benno's gauges are the honest document.
Fallback designation. Chalk marks: fourteen, a gap, six.
Fresh stencil. 12-C can cite it as a pool. The kit is water.
The kit is gone. The stencil is a levy map.
A condemned tag on a room with one dry motor.
One dry motor hums. The Drown lowers a step.
Condemned stands. Sublevels stay shut.
A window entry, a dusted room, a crate of plates string-tied.
The crate is open. Plates filed by number. Lived names are subtitles.
The crate stayed tied. Ostrowski's sheet is the one that matches the ground.
Cotton gloves that are not yours. The second-copy cage is empty.
The cage holds the Record. Sole filed it. Two witnesses.
The cage holds the lived map. Sole filed spoken names.
Both copies in the cage. Nobody likes either.
The cage is empty. Sole cannot complete ground.
